The repo binding written by 'entire brain connect' never refreshed, so once the bound repo was deleted or the caller lost access, every trigger (session-end hook, daemon tick, push hint) retried the same 403 indefinitely — 11 denials in 10 minutes tripped brainstore's auth-failure monitor.

## What changed

- factsync surfaces 403 as an ErrNoAccess sentinel on both wire calls (401 unchanged, so auth-plumbing breaks still reach the monitor).
- On a pull 403, the sync re-resolves placement once via 'entire repo view'. A different repo id in the same cell (deleted and re-onboarded) rebinds and retries; otherwise the binding records a 24h no-access pause ('no_access_until' in hosted.json) and prints one line naming 'entire brain connect'. The paused line prints only when the pause was actually recorded; a write declined by a concurrent connect/disconnect is silent.
- While paused, all background triggers skip silently, including the push hint before it claims its throttle. 'entire brain status' reports the pause. connect clears it by writing a fresh binding.
- All binding writes on this path go through a new locked read-modify-write (brainstore.MutateHostedRepoBinding) that re-checks opt-out and repo id, and never creates or repairs an absent or unreadable hosted.json.

## Deliberate deviations from the issue

- The pause keys off the pull 403, not any 403: a push-only denial is a real read-only-grant state (push 403, pull 200 — the COR-2030 staging smoke) and must keep pulling. All four stuck bindings 403 on the pull.
- Rebind requires the resolved cell URL to match the bound one, so an explicit --repo-id/--api-url binding (staging, non-default cell) is never silently retargeted.
